newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee exports on track despite crop disease.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee exports on track despite crop disease.

text.p: Uganda's coffee exports will reach between 3.8 million and 4.0 million bags in 1996/97 despite capricious weather and coffee disease, the Uganda Coffee Development Authority (UCDA) said on Friday.

UCDA Board Secretary William Naggaga told Reuters that exports in the first eight months of 1996/97 (Oct-May) were 3.17 million bags. Average exports of 250,000 bags per month in the remaining four months would get Uganda to the 4.0 million bag threshold, Naggaga added.
For the same period last year, Uganda exported 2.9 million bags of coffee and went on to export a record 4.2 million, according to Naggaga's figures.
"We are going to meet our export targets. We have also had good prices on average in the last six months so the market situation is reasonable," Naggaga said.
He said the price of Ugandan robustas had reached around 2,000 pounds per tonne from around 1,100 pounds last year.

Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni told parliament on Thursday that he would send troops to southwestern Uganda, which is worst affected by the coffee wilt disease that completely kills trees, to help salvage the situation.

He said many peasants needed help to uproot and burn affected trees before planting replacements. He added that he was obliged to act to eradicate a disease that could destroy all Uganda's coffee in just five years.
Naggaga said the situation was very serious. Some 11 key growing districts were affected, but the government had taken urgent measures to stem any further spread.
Measures included immediate destruction of affected trees and a ban on the transport of coffee from affected areas.
UCDA has also set aside 200 million shillings to help in a campaign against the disease and will host a major international conference on the disease next month.
Finance Minister Jehoash Mayanja-Nkangi told parliament on Thursday, "If our coffee wilts, this will mean a very big problem in the economy."
Coffee is Uganda's leading foreign exchange earner despite a campaign in the past five years to diversify. It accounts for as much as 70 percent of Uganda's hard currency earnings.
Uganda is Africa's leading exporter of coffee.
